To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a sheep liver enzyme was purified and characterized that hydrolyzed FAD, NADD, and NADP+ at the pyrophospho bond and was activated by Pi.

the enzyme hydrolyzed FAD at a rate that was increased by the addition of phosphate, that the enzyme was not a nucleotide pyrophosphate, that it was inhibited by AMP, and that the inhibition by AMP was abolished by the addition Pi.
the nucleoside triphosphate (NTP) pyrophosphatases of sheep liver are distinct from the NAD pyrophosphatages and are inhibited by NTPs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the partial purification, properties, and inhibition of a sheep liver nucleotide pyrophosphate.
the properties of a sheep enzyme that hydrolyzes dinucleotides to mononucleotides and nucleotides.
the isolation, purification, and characterization of an enzyme that catalyzed the hydrolysis at the pyrophosphoryl bond of dinucleotidic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sheep liver enzyme hydrolyzed dinuclcotides at the pyro-phosphate bond and that this hydrolysis occurred by a mechanism that differed from that of other pyrophosphatases.
the nucleotide pyrophosphate of sheep liver is a unique enzyme that is specific for dinucleotides and is activated by Pi.
the enzyme hydrolyzed dinuclcotides, NAD+ or NADP+ at the pyrophosphoric acid bond.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sheep liver enzyme that cleaves FAD to FMN and AMP is a nucleotide pyrophosphate.
this enzyme is an ATP-ase, and that the hydrolysis at the pyrophosphoric bond in dinucleotide substrates is an artifact of the assay procedure.
this sheep liver nucleotide pyrophosphate catalyzes the release of FMN from FAD and NAD+ or NADP+ at the pyrophosphatases bond.
The main takeaway from our work is that
this enzyme has a unique property of releasing the pyrophosphate moiety of dinucleotidyl substrates at a rate that is enhanced in the presence of ortho-phosphate.
the enzyme is a dinucleoside pyrophosphohydrolase and not a nucleoside diphosphatase.
we found that a nucleotide pyrophosphate enzyme can be purified from sheep liver.
